criterion: At least one CRC-valid marker frame, containing values only canary code could draw, decoded from an independent recording of the screen.
summary: One native run of NAT-022 canary-trig (RECOVERY image sha256 f2cc234a70e7b4f54eb3469567d523233e70f486a220005cb36da47c00bcec64, canary Image 572ebd0f33a03a7d07f663267301f97661f4e3f0051e0d9e8c3597b06385f89b) under decision 0010: full-hash write to /dev/block/sda18 with readback match, one adb reboot recovery at 2026-11-10T12:34:31Z, owner-filmed screen, stock RECOVERY restored by one NAT-013 session (full hash equals stock 96620b8b..., check_android pass, sys.boot_completed=1, user 0 present). The owner reported seeing stripes and a video was supplied. Host decoding (docs/procedures/nat-022/decode_video.py, an observation of a phone camera recording, not a console): between 2.1 s and 61.8 s of the recording 857 sampled frames decode as CRC-valid marker frames, no frame has two different values within a round, and the sequence is exactly the canary-trig loop order (CHECK, ENTRY, BOOTID0, BOOTID1, STAGE, REG0..9; four rounds of ~18.3 s). The screen goes dark at ~61.9 s. Decoded fields: CHECK 0xA5A5 (stack round trip ok), ENTRY 0x8900 = entry at EL2 with SCTLR M=0, C=0, I=1 (current EL) and EL1 SCTLR M=0, C=0, I=1, BOOTID CNTVCT[31:0]=0x1AE1D195 constant across rounds, STAGE 0x10 (canary C reached via call). DECON0 report (REG frames): GLOBAL_CON 0x113 at kick 6 and 0x133 at kicks 21 and 36 (bits 0, 1, 8 set: enabled, command mode, as the DT says; other bits not interpreted), TRIG_CON 0x3063->0x3062 across the SW-form kick and 0x3062->0x3063 across the HW-form kick (readback follows our writes: HW_TRIG_EN toggles, mask bit 4 clear, SW_TRIG_EN bit 8 not set in the readback), FRAME_COUNT (low 16 bits) 163->314 over the interval before kick 6, 1358->1358 before kick 21, 2407->2557 before kick 36; kick counts 6, 21, 36, matching the loop. Not established: that the DECON0 kick (rather than S-Boot's own refresh) made the markers visible (no control with identical decoding; the canary-plain run 001 had no camera decode and the owner's report there was only 'seemingly no stripes'), why FRAME_COUNT advances ~150 per ~1.2 s interval after HW-form kicks but 0 after the SW-form kick while SW-form frames were still displayed, the framebuffer stride/format (the visible band height of ~59 +/- 3 screen rows is consistent with the hypothesised 4320 B/row, an uncalibrated camera estimate not a measurement), the exception handler path (canary-fault not run), anything about XNU or the loader (not run). The host USB observer saw ADB vanish ~10.6 s and SEC_UPLOAD enumerate ~95 s after observer start with no command sent, the same pattern as run 001; the recording's clock was not aligned to it.
